3359144.title: Yongsan Youth Festival: Fancy a Rest?
3359144.overview: A one-day festival for young residents of Yongsan-gu built around the idea of rest — the programme is framed as emptying the mind, refilling energy and heading back out into the world. It runs in the former officers' quarters at Yongsan Park, the site handed back after more than a century of military use and now one of central Seoul's most unusual public spaces. The stage bill mixes dance crews, a gugak ensemble, magic and pop acts. Free.

2431706.title: Yongin Cyber Science Festival
2431706.overview: The 26th edition of Yongin's science festival, held over two days at Yongin Mir Stadium. Four themed zones cover future technology, a hands-on workshop, the future city and young scientists — with robot-arm demonstrations, humanoid robots and drones to pilot, future mobility to ride, and VR simulators. There are carbon-neutral energy experiments, making gadgets with Arduino and 3D pens, and a care robot to try. Samsung Electronics and other local companies show current work alongside school science clubs, a drone soccer class and character-based science kits. Free, with a materials charge on some activities.

4109893.title: Damyang Heritage Night Walk
4109893.overview: Damyang after dark, staged around Gwanbangjerim — a riverside forest planted in the 1600s to hold back floods and now a national monument — plus the stone flagpole supports at Gaeksa-ri and the five-storey pagoda at Namsan-ri. The programme tells the stories of people Damyang produced: a street play about the magistrate who built the forest, a madang changgeuk honouring Yi Nal-chi, the great Joseon pansori singer born here, a talk concert with piano beneath the flagpole supports, and a family mission built on the Taoist trickster Jeon U-chi, who is said to have trained at Damyang's Yeondongsa Temple. Free, with some market stalls and activities charged.
4109893.sponsor: Korea Heritage Service · Jeonnam-Gwangju · Damyang County

4109730.title: Independence Fair: Centenary of the June 10th Movement
4109730.overview: On 10 June 1926, crowds used the funeral procession of Sunjong — the last emperor of Korea — as cover to stage mass demonstrations against Japanese rule. 2026 marks a hundred years since. This fair at Andong International Convention Center recreates the scene in an exhibition zone, runs hands-on activities with veterans' organisations, and adds lectures and a talk show aimed at younger visitors, with outdoor performances alongside. Free.
